SddReadiness.keywords: readiness, setup, bootstrap, tooling, package-json, npm-scripts, gennady, stub, not-ready, proxy-handoff, sdd-readiness
SddReadiness.Mission:
Bring a not-ready repo to the point where the SDD flow can run: a `package.json` exists and declares the eight exact bricks `sdd-state` checks — `type-check` · `test` · `test:coverage` · `format` (read-only) · `format:fix` · `lint` (reaching `gennady`, read-only) · `lint:fix` · the public whole-project `fix`. Each real `*:fix` MUST declare an argument-forwarding prefix ending in a write switch (`--write` / `--fix` / `--autofix`; a non-mutating or obvious broad-root brick is a configuration error), and `fix` reaches formatter then linter — gennady is installed, and `READINESS` leaves `not-ready`: `ready` when every brick is a real tool, `provisional` when some are still stubs (the normal landing state of a from-scratch setup — see the stub template and the exit arms below). `check` is an optional read-only wrapper; phase agents pass exact Target Files to `sdd-verify`, whose private repair adapters pass capability-filtered exact subsets to the formatter, project linter, and Gennady contract linter, then enforce the actual write zone by a runtime workspace diff; static brick shape is only early diagnostics. Required `fix` is the single public whole-project repair entrypoint. This is the minimal mechanical bootstrap, NOT the tooling design: a real command where a tool is already installed, else a visible TODO stub that points at the infra flow. Entered when `sdd-state` reports `READINESS=not-ready` — from the router preflight or from any skill's own preflight. Self-sufficient: it may run without the router core in context, so it repeats the operator-facing axioms it needs.
Input — the `sdd-state` readiness verdict. Output — a `package.json` patched toward `ready`, plus a handed-over command list for anything that FAILED when the agent tried it (typically dependency installs the corporate proxy 403s).
Out of scope: choosing the real tool stack with a Decision Log (the infra branch), and the project portal (the root branch). This flow only makes the commands EXIST and runnable.
SddReadiness.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_OUTPUT_LIVE_TEXT, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, HALT_FORMAT, MESSAGE_LAYOUT, QUESTION_RULE_SLIM
External research (WebSearch/WebFetch) run in this session ALWAYS lands as a research document via `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug ` — filled in BEFORE the result feeds a proposal to the operator; a chat summary is not storage (session dies, research dies with it). Every factual claim must be re-verifiable: traced to a source (a specific page, URL + access date; for code-derived facts — path + commit) OR explicitly flagged `agent conclusion` / `from model memory as of `. A fact carrying neither is a document defect, not a style choice. A repeat question checks existing `specs/**/research/` first — supersede, never duplicate.
Prefer primary evidence: official documentation, repository/release notes, standards, or papers. A secondary comparison may supplement but never solely support a tool/version/API decision. The candidate analysis remains immutable after it is shown. Once the operator decides, update only `FINAL_DISPOSITION`: outcome, the actual spec/Decision Log choice, and its delta from the research recommendation. A later critic change updates the same disposition or marks the document superseded.
SddReadiness.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_SETUP` | Operator declines to set the project up. Without the required scripts no SDD branch can run — state that plainly and stop |

Step.Goal: State the honest readiness gap, straight from sdd-state.
Step.Action: Take everything from `sdd-state`'s `[READINESS]` block — `package.json` present/absent, each required script declared/not, `lint→gennady`, `check→read-only`, `gennady-installed` — plus the `missing` list (which now names `format(read-only)` and `lint(read-only)` separately from `check(read-only)` when a formatter/linter write switch leaks into that script's own chain). That tool is the single source of state (`AX_TOOL_INVOCATION`); do not re-derive it by hand. Tell the operator, in plain Russian (`AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`), exactly what is present and what is missing. No narration, just the gap. Flow into the plan (no STOP).

Step.Goal: Lay out the fix and get a go-ahead.
Step.Action:
From the `missing` list, lay out what will be done: patch `package.json` (real command where the tool is already a dependency, else a TODO stub), wire `lint` to `gennady`, keep `format` / `lint` read-only (any formatter/linter write switch moves to `format:fix` / `lint:fix`, each of which MUST carry one), seed required whole-project `fix` and optional read-only `check`, and install the missing dependencies / `gennady`. If the operator wants to lock a real tool now (test runner, formatter, type-checker) — a genuine NEW pick, not the stub path — first resolve its exact owning infrastructure scope from the caller's saved `sdd-state` Scopes/GATE_QUEUE snapshot. No owning infra scope means no toolchain research or choice in this bootstrap flow: seed the stub and defer the decision to infra. This is not an exception to persistence; it avoids producing ownerless evidence.
With an exact owning infra scope, run the research gate: 2–3 targeted WebSearch/external-doc queries (alive/current and AI-agent-friendly this year). Before any finding shapes the options, run exact researchManifest ToolCall below and fill the created document: source URL + access date in EVIDENCE, findings/trade-offs in the corresponding analysis sections, and FINAL_DISPOSITION linking the exact owning Tool Stack / Decision record when the operator chooses. Then offer 2–3 options with trade-offs (`AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND`), each rationale linked to that artifact. There is no bootstrap exception to `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED`, and no extra Ask: the existing plan Approval Check owns the choice. If WebSearch is unavailable, say so plainly — `предлагаю по памяти на <дата обучения модели>, ресёрч недоступен` — and create no fake research artifact. If no external research is used, make no research call/artifact. Otherwise stub it and defer the choice to infra. Present the plan + Approval Check (`AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT` — no edits before an explicit go-ahead). STOP. npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug Inputs , : =exact infrastructure scope from caller's saved sdd-state snapshot; =restricted slug for the one researched tool category; only after external research is actually used. Use researchManifest.

Step.Goal: Do everything the agent can — edits and installs.
Step.Action: With approval: create `package.json` if absent (name + `scripts`); add the eight exact bricks — real command where the tool exists, else the TODO stub (see Reference Data); `lint` always reaches `gennady`; `format` / `lint` stay read-only, while `format:fix` / `lint:fix` MUST each carry a real write switch (`--write` / `--fix` / `--autofix`) — a fixer that never mutates is a configuration error, flagged the same as a missing script; seed required whole-project `fix` = `format:fix` → `lint:fix` and optional read-only `check` = npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full; AND run the dependency installs the project needs (`npm i -D …`, gennady) — try them — the corporate proxy often blocks installs, but not always. Re-run exact readinessState ToolCall below. Anything that failed goes to STEP_3. npx gennady sdd-state Use readinessState.

Step.Goal: Report any failed command and hand it to the operator — once, no loop.
Step.Action: For each command that FAILED in STEP_2 (typically an install the proxy 403'd), immediately tell the operator the EXACT command that did not work and the error — once, no retry, no environment-fixing. Hand it over to run themselves. Present the failed-command block and wait (`HALT_FORMAT`-style). STOP until the operator runs them and says done («готово / дальше»).

WHEN `STEP_3_REPORT_FAILURES` ran (some command failed and the operator stepped in by hand) → re-run exact readinessState ToolCall below now — the operator's own actions changed state since STEP_2's snapshot, so it is stale. WHEN `STEP_3` was skipped (STEP_2 applied cleanly, nothing failed) → reuse STEP_2's own closing `sdd-state` re-run directly; it is already the fresh post-apply snapshot, and a second call here would just re-confirm it — a wasted turn. Either way: `READINESS=ready` → setup is done; return exact post-mutation alias `readinessState` to the caller (the router's preflight/route step, or the skill's own flow). `READINESS=provisional (stubs: …)` → ALSO done for this flow, and the expected landing state when the eight bricks were seeded from the stub template above: the skeleton exists, the real tools do not. Return control the same way, saying so in one line — name the stubbed scripts, and state that bootstrap/config/doc phases and `scaffold` may proceed while `impl`/`refactor`/`test`/`fix` phases stay mechanically refused until an infra ticket replaces those stubs. Do NOT loop back to `STEP_1` over stubs this flow just wrote by design, and never report `provisional` as `ready`. Still `not-ready` → state the remaining gap and resume at `STEP_1` for the leftover items only — a fresh assessment, never a blind re-run of a command that already failed. Every return from this directive carries exactly that one latest `readinessState`; the caller must reuse it and must not refresh again. npx gennady sdd-state Use readinessState only when STEP_3 ran; otherwise reuse STEP_2 readinessState.

SddReadiness.ReferenceData:
The eight exact bricks `sdd-state` checks (exact match — `type-check` also accepts the `typecheck` spelling, every other name has exactly one):
| script | purpose | stubbable until infra flow? | |---|---|---| | `type-check` | type-check, no emit | yes | | `test` | run tests | yes | | `test:coverage` | tests with coverage | yes | | `format` | formatter in check-only mode — read-only | yes | | `format:fix` | formatter write mode — MUST carry `--write` / `--fix` / `--autofix` | yes (stub still needs the literal switch — see below) | | `lint` | lint chain that reaches `gennady` (DbC), read-only | **no — must wire gennady** | | `lint:fix` | project-linter autofix prefix — MUST carry `--write` / `--fix` / `--autofix`; receives only its own ABI, never assumed Gennady flags | yes (same caveat) | | `fix` | public whole-project repair: `format:fix` then `lint:fix`, with broad roots supplied here | yes |
`format` and `lint` — and every script either reaches via `npm run ` — must stay free of known write switches (`eslint … --fix`, `prettier … --write`, `… --autofix`); a leaked write switch fails that script's own read-only check (`format(read-only)` / `lint(read-only)` in `missing`), even if every script name is present. A real `format:fix` / `lint:fix` declares an argument-forwarding command prefix: its write switch is the final token and no obvious broad root/glob is baked into the command. The phase appends exact Target Files; required whole-project `fix` supplies broad roots explicitly while reaching both leaves in order. This static, tool-agnostic shape check cannot prove that an arbitrary exact operand such as `src/a.ts` is a target rather than tool config/subcommand; the phase's runtime workspace boundary closes that ambiguity by rejecting and listing actual writes outside its canonical Target Files without rolling them back. A missing switch or obvious broad target reports in `missing`. Phase repair treats formatter, project linter, and Gennady contract lint as distinct capabilities: ESLint-like leaves receive only applicable exact code targets; Gennady receives `--include-tests`, owning `--spec`, and only supported `.ts`/`.tsx`. If `lint:fix` itself reaches Gennady it runs once for both lint roles; zero applicable targets are an explicit named skip, never a broad-root fallback. Bootstrap echo-stubs are the sole temporary exception because setup never executes them. Optional `check` is the human/CI wrapper: `"check": "npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full"` and must itself stay read-only.
A minimal `package.json` that reads as **`provisional`** once gennady is installed — real `lint`, the rest stubbed until the infra flow locks real tools (point `lint` at the project's own source dirs). `provisional` is a real, named state, not a lesser `ready`: the eight bricks are in place, so bootstrap/config/doc phases and `scaffold` may proceed — but `sdd-task --phase` mechanically REFUSES every `impl`/`refactor`/`test` phase (`ERR_CLI_SDD_TASK_INFRA_NOT_READY`) and a code/test phase call (`sdd-verify --task ... --phase ...`) and `--profile full` return `⛔` for a stubbed foundation, because an `echo` that exits 0 verifies nothing and a green verdict on it would be a fiction. Only replacing every stub with a real tool moves the project to `ready` (= execution-ready). The `format:fix`/`lint:fix` stubs below carry a literal `--fix`/`--write` token as a placeholder switch — a plain `echo TODO` alone would report as a non-mutating fixer even before a real tool is picked: ```json { "scripts": { "type-check": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (type-check — tsc --noEmit)' >&2", "test": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (test runner)' >&2", "test:coverage": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (coverage)' >&2", "format": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (formatter, read-only check)' >&2", "format:fix": "echo 'TODO: настроить formatter --write (write mode)' >&2", "lint": "gennady lint src/", "lint:fix": "echo 'TODO: настроить linter --fix (autofix)' >&2", "check": "npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full", "fix": "npm run format:fix -- . && npm run lint:fix -- src/" } } ``` `lint` may reach `gennady` directly or through an `npm run ` chain — either satisfies the `lint→gennady` check. The leaf stubs print a warning to stderr but **exit 0 — by design they pass the SHAPE checks**; `format`/`lint`/`check` stay read-only-clean since neither their own body nor anything they reach carries a write switch, while `format:fix`/`lint:fix` pass the mutating check on their placeholder token alone. A real replacement must become an declared argument-forwarding prefix; broad roots stay in required `fix`. That is what makes this package.json `provisional` rather than `ready`: shape is satisfied, substance is not. `sdd-state` names every stub it found on the READINESS line, and that list IS the infra flow's worklist — the project reaches `ready` exactly when the list is empty.
SddReadiness.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (`AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🧰 SETUP_R · package.json= · ready=` — the three-level verdict verbatim from `sdd-state`, never flattened to yes/no. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Assess · Plan · Apply · Ready.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
